name: Iron Mountain
description: Iron Mountain stores and manages physical records, media and (increasingly) digital information for about 240,000 customers in 61 countries, including about 95 percent of the Fortune 1000. Its core business, records and information management (RIM), charges monthly storage rent on more than 740 million cubic feet of stored material plus service fees for moving, retrieving, shredding and digitizing it. A second, fast-growing line leases data-center capacity (488 MW existing, 97 percent leased, total potential 1,340 MW) mostly to hyperscale customers. A third, in Corporate and Other, is asset lifecycle management (ALM: secure disposal and remarketing of IT hardware) and Fine Arts storage. Revenue grew 12.2 percent in FY2025 to $6.9 billion; RIM earned a 44.7 percent adjusted EBITDA margin and data centers 51.8 percent.

gics.note: Conventional label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC code is 6798 (Real Estate Investment Trusts). The box misleads: 41 percent of FY2025 revenue was 'service' revenue (pickup, delivery, shredding, digitization, IT asset disposition) rather than rent, most of the money comes from records-management contracts that renew like a subscription with annual price increases, and a fast-growing 11.6 percent slice is wholesale data-center leasing to hyperscalers, which resembles Equinix or Digital Realty.

businessLines.name: Global RIM Business
businessLines.how: Customers pay monthly storage rent per cubic foot (the 10-K credits organic storage rental growth to revenue management, i.e. pricing) plus service fees each time boxes are retrieved, delivered, shredded or digitized; storage rent is the profit engine and service revenue grows with digital and activity levels.
businessLines.description: Records and information management: physical records storage, secure shredding, digital solutions (Global Digital Solutions), and related services in North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific, run from 1,214 facilities.
